t: You're looking at a bronze statue of Spencer Cavendish, the 8th Duke of Devonshire, at the entrance to Horse Guards Avenue on Whitehall. It's a Grade II listed work by the sculptor Herbert Hampton, unveiled in 1911. Cavendish is remembered for something unusual: he led three different political parties, the Liberals, the Liberal Unionists and the Conservatives, between 1875 and 1903. He also declined to become prime minister on three occasions, because the circumstances were never right.
